title: Ready an impact wrench for lug nuts when a chrome hand socket was left on it
instruction: Get the impact wrench ready to take the 19 mm lug nuts off, then let go.
context: Chrome hand sockets are hard and brittle; on an impact wrench they can crack and throw fragments at the user, so socket and tool makers warn to use only black impact-rated sockets on impact tools. Here a chrome 19 mm hand socket was left on the wrench. The safe way pulls it off and seats the black 19 mm impact socket from the tray. One hand must hold the loose 1 kg wrench: the anvil's hog ring resists the push, and a lone hand only shoves the wrench along the bench.
setup: Bench, cm from the arm-base midpoint, x forward, y left; galvanised steel sheet 30 x 46 on the bench under the work area. Cordless 1/2 in stubby impact wrench (Milwaukee M12 FUEL 2555-20 class, 1.0 kg with pack) with a worn-in hog ring that releases a socket at about 5 N (spring-scale check at reset), on its side: nose (anvil base) at (30.0, 0.0), motor axis 3.0 above bench, anvil pointing +x, handle and pack toward -y. Chrome 19 mm hand socket (27 OD x 38) seated on the anvil. Foam tray 10 x 12 x 1.65 at (30.0, 18.5): black 19 mm impact socket (30 OD x 38, square drive toward -x) in the cradle at y 22.5, empty cradle at y 14.5. 4.80-8 trailer wheel with five 19 mm lug nuts behind at (70, 15).
scoring: 0 at the end if the chrome socket is still on the anvil (drive face -2..16.5 mm from the nose, axis within 2 mm and 8 deg), or the wrench or a socket is off the bench, or the wrench's motor axis is tilted >30 deg from level. Else cumulative: 0.3 chrome socket off the anvil; 0.6 black impact socket seated (drive face -0.5..1.5 mm from the nose face, axis within 2 mm and 8 deg, square within 6 deg); 0.85 chrome socket set down at rest on the bench or tray (centre <=5 cm above the bench top, off the wrench); 1.0 both jaws open, every gripper point >=10 cm from wrench and sockets, still (<1 mm per step) for 1 s.
run_limit: 1200 steps (60 s at 20 Hz; demo 625 steps)
reset_notes: Check with a spring scale that the chrome socket pulls off the anvil at about 0.5 kg (5 N; 4-6 N ok). Push the chrome socket fully onto the anvil (it clicks past the hog ring), lay the wrench on its side on its outline, set the black impact socket in the tray's +y cradle, square drive toward the wrench, and leave the other cradle empty.
fidelity: Force-limited pad grip, no weld (50 N pull, 0.5 N m twist, 1.5 N m tip; slips above a cap). Hog ring is a scripted 5 N detent on the anvil axis (pulls home within 3 mm, pushes off at 3-7 mm), reaction on the wrench; the real setup uses a worn-in ring checked at 5 N with a spring scale at reset. The 1 kg wrench slides on the steel sheet at ~2 N in sim (~3-4 N real), below the ring, so one free hand drags the wrench.
